desc:
A second pair of eyes finds what the author cannot see. Ecom Swift LLC provides a code review for SaaS and web apps: a written report on quality, speed and security, with findings ranked by priority and examples taken from your own files.

## What is a code review for a SaaS app?

A code review is a careful reading of your source code by an experienced developer who did not write it. The reviewer looks at structure, readability, tests, slow spots and common security mistakes, then reports what should change and in which order.

It is different from a security audit or a penetration test. Those probe a running system for weaknesses. A review reads the code itself and tells you where it is hard to maintain, slow, fragile or risky, and what is already done well.

## Why a review is worth having

Code written under deadline pressure tends to carry the same patterns: long functions, copied logic, unclear names, missing tests, secrets in the wrong place. The team that wrote it has stopped noticing them. A new hire, an investor, an acquirer or a future contractor will notice them immediately.

A review gives you an honest picture before those people arrive. It also settles internal arguments. When two developers disagree about whether a module needs rework, an outside report with examples gives the team a shared starting point.

## How a review improves speed, quality and cost

The benefit shows up in time. Clean, tested code is faster to change, so features ship sooner and break less. Slow queries and wasteful requests, found early, keep hosting bills and page times down as usage grows. Security slips, such as missing input checks or weak session handling, are far cheaper to close before they are exploited than after.

The ranked list matters as much as the findings. Teams rarely lack ideas for improvement. They lack a way to decide what comes first. A report that separates urgent risks from long-term tidying lets you act this week without stopping all other work.

## What a useful review report contains

- A short summary of the overall state of the code, in plain language.
- Findings grouped by area: structure, naming, errors, tests, speed and security.
- A priority label on each finding, from fix now to fix when convenient.
- Real code examples from your repository, with a suggested better version.
- Notes on dependencies that are outdated or unused.
- A check for secrets, keys and credentials committed to the code.
- A view of test coverage and which risky areas have none.
- Things the team does well, so good habits are kept.
- A call to walk through the report and answer questions.

## How we work

You give us read access to the code, or to the part of it you want reviewed. We read it in context, run it where we can and note issues as we go. We then sort the findings, write the report and book a call to go through it with you.

The Basic package reviews one area of the code and returns ranked quality notes. Standard covers a wider area with speed hot spots, common security checks and a walkthrough call. Premium adds a dependency and secrets check, a test coverage review, a ranked fix plan with effort and a few findings fixed as worked examples. We change nothing in your code unless you ask us to.

## What to do, and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Tell us which area worries you most.
- Share any architecture notes, even rough ones.
- Include your test setup and how to run it.
- Invite the developers who wrote the code to the call.
- Treat the report as a plan, not a verdict.

**Avoid:**
- Cleaning up the code just before we read it, which hides the real state.
- Expecting a formal security certification from a review.
- Sending the entire repository when only one service matters.
- Acting on every finding at once.
- Ignoring the notes on what already works.

## Who this is for

This suits a founder who hired freelancers and wants to know what was actually built. It suits a team preparing for due diligence or a handover. It also suits a developer who wants an outside opinion on code written with assistant tools, where the output works but nobody fully understands it.

## What we need from you

Send a repository link and invite us as a collaborator with read access, or share an archive of the files in scope. Add a short description of what the app does and which parts matter most. We never need passwords, and we do not need access to production data to read code.
